```{python}
#| echo: false

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from pathlib import Path

from dih_models.plotting.chart_style import (
    setup_chart_style, add_watermark, clean_spines,
    COLOR_BLACK, COLOR_WHITE, add_png_metadata, get_figure_output_path,
    get_tick_formatter
)
from dih_models.parameters import format_parameter_value

setup_chart_style()

# Display name for chart title

display_name = "Expected Attributable Suffering Hours from One Prize Instance"

# Baseline and units

baseline = 1931098485636.3528

# Tornado data from sensitivity analysis

drivers = ['HOST_PRIZE_INSTANCE_DELTA_IMPLEMENTATION_PROBABILITY', 'NEW_DISEASE_FIRST_TREATMENTS_PER_YEAR', 'RARE_DISEASES_COUNT_GLOBAL', 'EVENTUALLY_AVOIDABLE_DALY_PCT', 'DFDA_PRAGMATIC_TRIAL_COST_PER_PATIENT', 'GLOBAL_YLD_PROPORTION_OF_DALYS', 'GLOBAL_ANNUAL_DALY_BURDEN', 'CURRENT_TRIAL_SLOTS_AVAILABLE', 'EFFICACY_LAG_YEARS', 'DFDA_OPEX_PLATFORM_MAINTENANCE', 'DFDA_OPEX_STAFF', 'DFDA_OPEX_INFRASTRUCTURE', 'DFDA_OPEX_REGULATORY', 'DFDA_OPEX_COMMUNITY']
driver_labels = ['Incremental Implementation Probability from One Prize Instance', 'Diseases Getting First Treatment Per Year', 'Total Number of Rare Diseases Globally', 'Eventually Avoidable DALY Percentage', 'dFDA Pragmatic Trial Cost per Patient', 'YLD Proportion of Total DALYs', 'Global Annual DALY Burden', 'Annual Global Clinical Trial Participants', 'Regulatory Delay for Efficacy Testing Post-Safety Verification', 'Decentralized Framework for Drug Assessment Maintenance Costs', 'Decentralized Framework for Drug Assessment Staff Costs', 'Decentralized Framework for Drug Assessment Infrastructure Costs', 'Decentralized Framework for Drug Assessment Regulatory Coordination Costs', 'Decentralized Framework for Drug Assessment Community Support Costs']
impacts_low = [-1737988637072.7175, 1624319194160.3757, -265194970475.1631, -888701753273.1176, 146764498211.54224, -148546037356.64282, -100578046126.89307, 34500055374.12036, -18227729831.7583, 37646511.14794922, 22589982.497314453, 22589982.497314453, 15060680.362792969, 7530686.228759766]
impacts_high = [17379886370727.174, -928182396663.0717, 795584911425.4905, 111999109795.58838, -365323648793.39453, 148546037356.64258, 100578046126.8938, -34500055374.11987, 18227729831.758545, -52734190.28100586, -37663815.91040039, -30129667.774902344, -22596212.21142578, -7531378.419433594]

# Convert deltas to absolute values (baseline + delta)

values_low = [baseline + delta for delta in impacts_low]
values_high = [baseline + delta for delta in impacts_high]

# Create tornado chart (horizontal bars showing swing range)
# Cap dimensions to avoid LaTeX "Dimension too large" errors in PDF output
# 8x10 inches max keeps figures compact and PDF-compatible

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, min(10, max(5, len(drivers) * 0.6))))

y_pos = np.arange(len(drivers))

# Plot low impact (left side)

for i, (low, high) in enumerate(zip(values_low, values_high)):
    left = min(low, high)
    width_low = baseline - left if left < baseline else 0
    width_high = max(low, high) - baseline if max(low, high) > baseline else 0

    # White bar for range below baseline

    if width_low > 0:
        ax.barh(i, width_low, left=left,
                color=COLOR_WHITE, edgecolor=COLOR_BLACK, linewidth=2)

    # Black bar for range above baseline

    if width_high > 0:
        ax.barh(i, width_high, left=baseline,
                color=COLOR_BLACK, edgecolor=COLOR_BLACK, linewidth=2)

# Format axis

ax.set_yticks(y_pos)
# Simplified labels (just parameter names)

ax.set_yticklabels(driver_labels, fontsize=11)
ax.set_title(f'Sensitivity Analysis: {display_name}', fontsize=16, weight='bold', pad=20)

# X-axis label with units

units_label = "hours"
if units_label:
    ax.set_xlabel(f'{display_name} ({units_label})', fontsize=12)
else:
    ax.set_xlabel(f'{display_name}', fontsize=12)

# Format x-axis tick labels with K/M/B/T notation

ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(get_tick_formatter(unit=units_label))

# Add vertical line at baseline

ax.axvline(baseline, color=COLOR_BLACK, linewidth=1, linestyle='--', alpha=0.5)

# Clean spines

clean_spines(ax)

# Add watermark

add_watermark(fig)

# Save PNG to knowledge/figures/ regardless of where Quarto renders from
# Use 96 DPI for web-optimized output (reduced from 150 DPI to minimize file size)

output_path = get_figure_output_path('tornado-host_prize_instance_expected_attributable_suffering_hours.png')
plt.savefig(output_path, dpi=96, bbox_inches=None, facecolor=COLOR_WHITE)

add_png_metadata(
    output_path,
    title=f'Sensitivity: {display_name}',
    description=f'Tornado diagram showing which input parameters have the largest impact on {display_name}'
)

plt.show()
```
